title: Quotients of universally catenary Noetherian rings
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian universally catenary ring and let $I\subset A$ be any ideal. Then $A/I$ is universally catenary. [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-exc-excellent-ring]

proof.text: Put $R=A/I$ and let $\pi:A\to R$ be the quotient map. To verify that $R$ is Noetherian using [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $J$ be an arbitrary ideal of $R$. Its inverse image $K=\{a\in A:\pi(a)\in J\}$ is an ideal of $A$, hence has finitely many generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$. Their images generate $J$: each $y\in J$ lifts to some $a\in K$ by surjectivity of $\pi$, and an expression $a=\sum b_i a_i$ gives $y=\sum\pi(b_i)\pi(a_i)$. Conversely all these generators lie in $J$. Thus every ideal of $R$ is finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian. This writes out the quotient argument in Stacks Tag 00FN, proof of lemma-Noetherian-permanence.

Let $B$ be any finite type $R$-algebra. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], choose generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ such that every element of $B$ is a polynomial in them with coefficients in $R$. Give $B$ its $A$-algebra structure by composing $A\xrightarrow{\pi}R\to B$. For any such polynomial expression, lift each of its finitely many coefficients from $R$ to $A$ along $\pi$. Evaluating the lifted polynomial at the same $b_i$ gives the same element of $B$. Therefore the same finite set generates $B$ as an $A$-algebra, and $B$ is of finite type over $A$. This is the finite-type composition argument in lemma-universally-catenary, written out for a quotient base; it does not require $I$ to be prime or proper.

source.place: Tag 00NK, lemma-quotient-catenary, second assertion; Tag 0ECE, proof of lemma-universally-catenary, finite-type case; Tag 00F3, definition-finite-type (1)

proof.text: By the universally catenary clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring], the hypothesis on $A$ says that every finite type $A$-algebra is catenary. Apply it to the $A$-algebra $B$ of Step 2. Thus every finite type $R$-algebra $B$ is catenary. Together with the Noetherian property proved in Step 1, this is exactly universal catenarity of $R=A/I$ under the same definition (Stacks Tag 00NL). The ring $B$ and its prime chains are unchanged on restricting scalars, so both the bound on finite chain lengths and equality of saturated-chain lengths hold for the required ring.
